drawings.description: Croquis : à gauche, les trois $V_0^\circ$, $V_1^\circ$, $V_2^\circ$, avec $\partial V_1^\circ \to V_0^\circ$ et $\partial V_2^\circ = \partial_1 V_2^\circ \cup \partial_0 V_2^\circ$ envoyé sur $V_1^\circ$ et $V_0^\circ$ par des flèches courbes ; en bas, un tableau de flèches $\partial_2 \leftarrow \partial_{21}$, $\partial_{20} \leftarrow \partial_{210}$, $\partial_1 \leftarrow \partial_{10}$, $\partial_0 \leftarrow \ldots$, avec « bord » ; deux bandes hachurées étiquetées $\partial_{210}$, $\partial_{20}$, $\partial_{21}$ ; un cylindre et un tore étiquetés $\partial_{10}$, $\partial_1$ ; un grand cercle $\partial_0$ contenant une haltère $\partial_0$ ; dans un cadre, $\partial_1$, $\partial_{10}$, $\partial_0 = \partial_0$, et un demi-cercle posé sur un segment, marqué $\partial_1\ \partial_0\ \partial_1$
drawings.kind: page of sketches: V_i^o with boundary maps, table of boundary arrows, bands, cylinder, circle with dumbbell, framed figure
drawings.notes: Lower half of the sheet (the formulas above are text). The scheme V_0^o, V_1^o, V_2^o with the arrows from their boundaries is kept from the earlier redraw (its overlay is close). The rest is redrawn on tight crops: the table of arrows d_2 <- d_21, d_20 <- d_210, d_1 <- d_10, d_1 <- d_10, d_0 <- d_0 at the places where he wrote them, "bord" twice, the four curved arrows to the left, the curve from the second "bord" and the two downward arrows through the table (their sources and targets remain a reading); the two hatched bands with their four corner points (computed once, the edges drawn from them) and their labels, a long hatching stroke beyond the first band; the cylinder (a cap and four lines along it) and the small tube (a ring with two lines), labels d_10, d_1 and the dotted d's; the large circle d_0 with the dumbbell, its two bars ending on the two rings; the frame (a line along the top, the right side, a small bracket with d), d_1, d_10, d_0 = d_0, and the half-circle on a segment with three points on the line below and its labels d_1 d_0 d_1. Labels at \small, drawing at 2 mm per unit. Left out: the scribbled fan at the lower right of the frame (overinked, with d_1 beside it), the struck mark before the last d_0 of the table, the squiggles after "bord", the name written at the top of the sheet (Fujii Guruji Nichidatsu, a public religious figure), which is not part of the mark. Still differs: the curved arrows of the table and the tube are approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): every figure of the plate laid over the scan rendered at 350 dpi in colour, in zoomed parts (18-62 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script. The table of arrows (its straight and curved arrows), the two hatched bands, the frame with the half-circle and the dumbbell lie on their ink within about 1 unit and were left as they were. Corrected: the cylinder, re-read at 62 px a unit, is a cap drawn as one open loop from the heavy line round the left, a thin top line, the heavy line, a third line and a doubled bottom line, with the two small arcs across it between the top and the heavy line (the old cap and lines were 1 to 2 units off); the small tube gets the short stroke across its ring and the dash to its left, its lower line starts at the ring's foot, and its d_1 moved 1 unit right; the large circle d_0 is drawn as the open loop it is (open at the lower right, with a small curl at the top) instead of an ellipse; the dumbbell's bars and the lower dotted d_0 moved onto their ink; in the scheme V_0^o, V_1^o, V_2^o the long curved arrow from d_1V_2^o u d_0V_2^o to V_0^o follows its ink (it ran 1 to 2 units high) and the arrow from dV_1^o moved onto its ink. Left out as before: the scribbled fan at the lower right of the frame (overinked, read as a crossing-out), the struck mark before the last d_0 of the table, the squiggles after « bord », the name at the top of the sheet; also the small ticks and figures written along the lower lines of the cylinder (unread writing). Added: the doubled oblique stroke with a dot that crosses the first « bord » between d_210 and d_10 (what it stands for is not read). The hatching of the bands is rendered as a pattern, not stroke by stroke.

drawings.description: page de dessins : une suite de figures numérotées 1°) à 6°) (un point $U_0$, puis $U_0$ et $U_0'$, des « haltères », des régions hachurées $V^{\circ\prime}$, $U''$), marquées I et II. En haut, la tour $U_0 \subset U_1 \subset U_2 \subset U_3 \ldots U_n$, avec $U_1^{\circ}$, $U_2^{\circ}$, $U_3^{\circ}$, $\partial U_1^{\circ} = U_0'$, $\partial U_2^{\circ}$, $U_1^{\circ\prime}$, $U_0''$, $\partial U_1^{\circ\prime} = \partial U''$, $U_2^{\circ\prime}$, $\partial U_2^{\circ\prime}$. À droite, un schéma vertical :
drawings.kind: page of drawings: tower U_0 in U_1 in ..., boundary scheme, dumbbells, regions I and II, figures 1o)-6o)
drawings.notes: Whole sheet, at 2 mm per unit with the labels at \small. Top left, the tower U_0 in U_1 in U_2, U_3 with U_i^o, their boundaries, U_1^o', U_0'', U_2^o' and the arrows (curved arrows approximate); top right the vertical scheme U_n -> U_n^o <- dU_n^o -> d_{n-1}U_n^o, ..., d_0U_n^o -> U_{n-1}^o, ..., U_0^o = U_0. Left column: the two dumbbells are redrawn on a tight crop: the first with its two rings open towards the bars, the two outer bars ending on the rings and the heavy bar between the two points; the second with its three bars ending on the two (hatched) rings and the two strokes from the points down to the apex, with two points on them; then a triangle, two segments, a small knob on three lines, and the large figure with U'', V^o, V^o', U' (hatched bar). Right: a dumbbell with strokes marked I and II inside a large pencil circle, a hatched fan, and the numbered sequence 1o)-6o) (U_0, U_0', U_1^o, hatched regions), schematised; many of its small labels are left out. An ink blot at the left is not drawn. Still differs (kept from the earlier redraw, overlay off by 1 to 3 units): the dumbbell with I and II and its pencil circle, the rings of the U'' figure (drawn too large), the hatched fans and the sequence 1o)-6o), whose many small labels U_0', U_1^o are left out. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the remaining differences named here (U'' rings, the I/II dumbbell, the sequence 1o)-6o)) are offsets of 1 to 3 units in a whole-page figure; they change no element of it, and the record stays partial for them. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): the whole sheet laid over the scan rendered at 350 dpi in colour; not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script; nothing changed. On their ink within about 1 to 2 units: the tower and its arrows, the vertical scheme, the two dumbbells of the left column with the triangle under the second, the triangle, the segments and the knob on three lines. Still differs, and the record stays partial for it: the U'' figure (its two outer loops are hatched freehand loops on the page, drawn as circles up to 3 units too large, and its hatched bar is a pattern fill); the dumbbell with I and II (rings and strokes 1 to 3 units off, the large pencil circle about 2 units up and to the left of its ink); the hatched fans, drawn as filled triangles where the page has fans of strokes; and the sequence 1o)-6o), which is schematised: most of its small labels (U_0', U_1^o, U_1^o', U_2^o and the others written beside the points and fans) are left out, and the circle of 5o) is about 2 units off. Redrawing these is the remaining work.

drawings.description: en haut à gauche, trois dessins l'un sous l'autre : un point « $V_0$ » ; une droite horizontale portant le point $V_0$ entre deux petits traits verticaux, « $V_1$ » de part et d'autre, deux petites flèches vers les traits et la légende « $\partial V_1 = V_{1,0}$ » ; une figure plane : la droite épaisse $V_1$ et son point $V_0$, bordée de deux traits parallèles qui contournent $V_0$ par deux arcs, les bandes marquées $V_{21}$, $V_{210}$, $V_{20}$, la région hachurée au-dessus et au-dessous marquée $V_2$.
drawings.kind: stratified neighbourhoods: a point, a line through it, a plane figure
drawings.notes: Three figures. (1) A point labelled V_0. (2) A horizontal line carrying the point V_0 between two short heavy vertical ticks, a small tick further left; V_1 written under each half of the line; two small arrows pointing up to the ticks, and under them the legend dV_1 = V_{1,0}. (3) The plane figure: a heavy middle line (V_1 on both halves) with the point V_0 and two small points on either side of it; a parallel line above and one below, each leaving its level to go round V_0 by an arc (the lower arc heavy and doubled), with a point at each end of each arc; labels V_{21}, V_{210}, V_{20}, V_{210}, V_{21} above and the same below; oblique hatching strokes above and below, and V_2 under the figure. Partial: the superscripts of V_0 (top) and of the two V_1 and of dV_1 are overwritten or struck scribbles and are left out; the hatching strokes are placed by eye (seven above, six below, as on the page); the arcs are drawn as circular arcs between their computed end points. The small arrow diagram at the right of the page (dV_1 = V_{10} -> V_0, and an arrow down to V_1) is a relation to be set as text and is not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the marks above V_0 (top), beside the two V_1 and on dV_1 are scribbles over struck superscripts; the legend is read dV_1 = V_{1,0} as in the transcription, and they stay left out. The faint traces of p. 45 are the mirror image of the ink drawings of p. 44 (compared on the two facsimiles, one flipped): set-off, not a sketch, so p. 45 gets no mark. Not checked by a reader. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the three figures, the arcs, the hatching strokes and the labels match the page within about 1 to 2 units; nothing corrected. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): re-read on millimetre grids of the scan rendered at 350 dpi in colour (15 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script and laid over the crop. The lines, ticks, arcs, points and labels lie on their ink within about 1 unit; the thirteen hatching strokes, which lay up to 4 units off, were each re-read at both ends and now lie on their ink. The struck superscripts stay left out (struck, as settled on 12 November); the arrow diagram at the right of the page is text.

drawings.description: au milieu à gauche, la tour encadrée : « $X_0 =$ » devant les cases $[\Phi_0]$, $[\Phi_1]$, $[\Phi_2]$, des flèches montant vers $X_1$ et $X_2$ ; au-dessous $\partial\Phi_1$ et $\partial\Phi_2$, la case $[(\partial_0\Phi_2)]$, $(\partial_1\Phi_2)$ et les cases $[(\partial_1\Phi_2)_0]$, $[(\partial_1\Phi_2)_1]$, avec $\Psi_0$, $\Psi_1$ et $\partial(\partial_1\Phi_2)_1$ ; de longues flèches courbes, chacune marquée d'un petit cercle, vont vers $[\Phi_0]$ et $[\Phi_1]$.
drawings.kind: boxed tower X_0 -> X_1 -> X_2 with ringed arrows
drawings.notes: The tower as drawn on the page, middle left: X_0 = in front of three boxes [Phi_0], [Phi_1], [Phi_2]; an arrow from [Phi_0] up to X_1 and from X_1 up to X_2; a heavy arrow from [Phi_1] up to X_1, an arrow from [Phi_2] up to X_2, and a long arrow from beside dPhi_2 up to X_1 (the attaching map dPhi_2 -> X_1, as read). Below: dPhi_1 with an arrow up to [Phi_1] (a small square drawn across its shaft), dPhi_2 with an arrow up to [Phi_2]; the box [(d_0Phi_2)] with an arrow up to dPhi_2, and an arrow towards dPhi_2 from the right, from (d_1Phi_2); (d_1Phi_2), unboxed, with arrows up to it from the boxes [(d_1Phi_2)_0] and [(d_1Phi_2)_1]; the lower edge of [(d_1Phi_2)_1] is an arrow pointing right, followed by two short strokes and Psi_1; two short strokes and Psi_0 under [(d_1Phi_2)_0]; d(d_1Phi_2)_1 with an arrow up to [(d_1Phi_2)_1] (a small square across its shaft). Arrows marked by a small ring on their shaft: dPhi_1 -> [Phi_0] (short), [(d_0Phi_2)] -> [Phi_0], [(d_1Phi_2)_0] -> [Phi_0] (long arc round the left), [(d_1Phi_2)_1] -> [Phi_1] (long arc over the top, crossing [Phi_2]), and d(d_1Phi_2)_1 -> [(d_1Phi_2)_0] (short). Boxes drawn as he drew them (the left side of [(d_1Phi_2)_0] and of [(d_1Phi_2)_1] are separate strokes, their lower edges are not closed against the sides). Still differs: free strokes placed from the 400 dpi colour crop, curved arrows drawn smooth through points read on it; what the small squares across two shafts and the two short strokes before Psi_0 and Psi_1 stand for is not read. The other three schemas of the page are relations to be set as text (given in the report of the finishing pass, scratchpad rmisc-report). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): laid over the scan rendered at 350 dpi in colour, whole and in zoomed parts (15-29 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script. Every box, arrow, ring, small square and label lies on its ink to within about 1 unit; nothing corrected. Left out: a faint broken vertical stroke under the left side of [(d_1Phi_2)_1], beside the arrow from d(d_1Phi_2)_1 (erased or set-off). What the small squares across two shafts and the two short strokes before Psi_0 and Psi_1 stand for is a question of reading, not of drawing: they are drawn where they are.
